documents.title: Artificial Intelligence: A Brief History
documents.text: Artificial intelligence was founded as an academic discipline in 1956 by John McCarthy, Marvin Minsky, Allen Newell, and Herbert Simon at the Dartmouth Conference. The field has gone through several waves of enthusiasm and disappointment, known as AI winters. In the 1950s and 1960s, early AI programs like ELIZA, created by Joseph Weizenbaum at MIT in 1966, demonstrated natural language processing. The expert systems of the 1970s and 1980s represented the first commercial success of AI. MYCIN, developed at Stanford University by Edward Shortliffe in 1976, used approximately 600 rules to diagnose bacterial infections and recommend antibiotics. Neural networks experienced a renaissance in the 1980s with the development of backpropagation by David Rumelhart, Geoffrey Hinton, and Ronald Williams in 1986. The modern deep learning era began in 2012 when Alex Krizhevsky, Ilya Sutskever, and Geoffrey Hinton won the ImageNet competition with AlexNet. Google DeepMind's AlphaGo, created by Demis Hassabis and David Silver, defeated world Go champion Lee Sedol in March 2016. In 2017, the transformer architecture was introduced by Vaswani et al. at Google in the paper Attention Is All You Need. OpenAI released GPT-3 in June 2020 with 175 billion parameters. ChatGPT, launched by OpenAI in November 2022, reached 100 million users within two months. Anthropic was founded in 2021 by Dario Amodei and Daniela Amodei. Meta AI released LLaMA in February 2023. NVIDIA's GPUs became the standard hardware for training large AI models. Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) emerged as an important technique for grounding language models in external knowledge.

documents.title: Quantum Computing: Principles and Applications
documents.text: Quantum computing harnesses quantum mechanical phenomena such as superposition and entanglement to process information. Richard Feynman proposed in 1982 that a quantum system could simulate physics more efficiently than a classical computer. David Deutsch at Oxford University formalized the concept of a universal quantum computer in 1985. A qubit can exist in a superposition of states simultaneously. Quantum entanglement is a phenomenon where two qubits become correlated regardless of distance. Peter Shor developed his famous factoring algorithm in 1994. Lov Grover developed a quantum search algorithm in 1996. IBM launched its Quantum Network in 2019. Google claimed quantum supremacy in 2019 when its Sycamore processor with 53 qubits completed a calculation in 200 seconds. IonQ, founded by Christopher Monroe in 2015, uses trapped ion technology. Rigetti Computing, founded by Chad Rigetti in 2013, develops superconducting quantum processors. PsiQuantum, founded by Jeremy O'Brien in 2016, pursues a photonic approach. Quantum error correction requires many physical qubits to create one logical qubit. NIST standardized post-quantum cryptographic algorithms in 2024, including CRYSTALS-Kyber and CRYSTALS-Dilithium.

documents.title: Space Exploration: From Sputnik to Mars
documents.text: The space age began on October 4, 1957, when the Soviet Union launched Sputnik 1, designed by Sergei Korolev. On April 12, 1961, Yuri Gagarin became the first human in space aboard Vostok 1. Alan Shepard became the first American in space on May 5, 1961. John Glenn became the first American to orbit Earth on February 20, 1962. President John F. Kennedy announced on September 12, 1962, that the United States would land a man on the Moon before the end of the decade. On July 20, 1969, Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin landed on the Moon during Apollo 11, while Michael Collins orbited above. The Space Shuttle program operated from 1981 to 2011 with 135 missions. The Hubble Space Telescope was launched on April 24, 1990, and is named after Edwin Hubble. The International Space Station has been continuously occupied since November 2, 2000. The Mars Exploration Rovers Spirit and Opportunity landed in January 2004. NASA's Curiosity rover landed on Mars on August 6, 2012. SpaceX, founded by Elon Musk in 2002, developed reusable Falcon 9 rockets. Blue Origin, founded by Jeff Bezos in 2000, developed the New Shepard vehicle. The James Webb Space Telescope launched on December 25, 2021. NASA's Perseverance rover landed on Mars on February 18, 2021, with the Ingenuity helicopter. The Artemis program aims to return humans to the Moon. China's Chang'e 4 landed on the far side of the Moon in January 2019.
